15 Healthy Pumpkin Recipes for Fall

When pumpkin season rolls around, there are so many delicious ways to use this versatile fall favorite. And while pumpkin pie definitely deserves a place at the table, pumpkin can do so much more!

We’ve gathered 15 of our favorite healthy pumpkin recipes for breakfast, snacks, dinner, and dessert. You’ll find cozy pumpkin pancakes and muffins, hearty pumpkin chili, creamy mac and cheese, pumpkin ravioli, and plenty of sweet fall treats.

15 Healthy Pumpkin Recipes Your Family Will Love

Most of these recipes use canned pumpkin puree, making them easy to prepare even when you don’t have a fresh pumpkin sitting on the counter. They’re also family-friendly, kid-approved, and perfect for bringing a little extra fall flavor into your kitchen.

Whether you’re trying to finish an open can of pumpkin or you’re ready to fully embrace pumpkin season, there’s something here for everyone.

1. Pumpkin Scones with Maple Drizzle

Tender, warmly spiced, and finished with a simple maple drizzle, these Pumpkin Scones with Maple Drizzle make a delicious fall breakfast or after-school snack. Pumpkin puree keeps the scones soft and moist, while cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves give them classic fall flavor.

They’re also freezer-friendly, making them a great recipe to bake ahead for busy mornings.

Get the Pumpkin Scones with Maple Drizzle recipe

2. Healthy Pumpkin Muffins

You can never have too many muffin recipes—especially when pumpkin is involved. These Healthy Pumpkin Muffins are made with whole wheat flour and pumpkin puree, with warm spices and mini chocolate chips for a kid-friendly finishing touch.

They’re easy to grab for breakfast, tuck into a lunchbox, or serve as an after-school snack. Make a double batch and freeze the extras for later.

Get the Healthy Pumpkin Muffins recipe

3. High Protein Pumpkin Pancakes

Bring pumpkin season to the breakfast table with these High Protein Pumpkin Pancakes. Greek yogurt adds protein while pumpkin puree gives the pancakes moisture, color, and delicious fall flavor.

Serve them with fresh fruit and a little maple syrup for an easy weekend breakfast the whole family can enjoy.

Get the High Protein Pumpkin Pancakes recipe

4. Pumpkin Streusel Oat Muffins

These Pumpkin Streusel Oat Muffins are soft, moist, and packed with cozy pumpkin spice flavor. Hearty oats and real pumpkin puree go into the muffins, while a buttery cinnamon-oat streusel adds a delicious crunchy topping.

They’re wholesome enough for breakfast, sweet enough for an after-school snack, and easy to freeze for another day.

Get the Pumpkin Streusel Oat Muffins recipe

5. Pumpkin Waffles

Crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and filled with pumpkin flavor, these Pumpkin Waffles are another fun way to bring fall to breakfast.

Top them with sliced bananas, chopped pecans, Greek yogurt, nut butter, or a drizzle of pure maple syrup for a cozy breakfast everyone can customize.

Get the Pumpkin Waffles recipe

6. Baked Pumpkin Oatmeal

If a warm bowl of oatmeal isn’t your kid’s favorite, try baking it instead! Baked Pumpkin Oatmeal combines rolled oats, pumpkin, and cozy autumn spices in a soft, sliceable breakfast.

It’s a great make-ahead option for busy school mornings and can also double as an easy lunchbox or after-school snack.

Get the Baked Pumpkin Oatmeal recipe

7. Protein Pumpkin Spice Dip

This sweet and creamy Protein Pumpkin Spice Dip tastes like pumpkin pie but makes a fun, protein-packed fall snack.

It’s made with pumpkin, chickpeas, almond butter, honey, and warm spices and comes together in about 10 minutes. Serve it with crisp apple or pear slices, whole-grain crackers, or toast for dipping.

Get the Protein Pumpkin Spice Dip recipe

8. Pumpkin Hummus

Pumpkin doesn’t have to be sweet! This Pumpkin Hummus blends pumpkin with chickpeas, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, and paprika for an easy savory snack.

Serve it with sliced cucumbers, carrots, snap peas, pita bread, or crackers. You can even shape it like a pumpkin for a festive Halloween or fall snack board.

Get the Pumpkin Hummus recipe

9. Pumpkin Ravioli with Brown Butter Sauce

Pumpkin is delicious at dinnertime, too! This Pumpkin Ravioli with Brown Butter Sauce combines tender pumpkin-filled ravioli with nutty brown butter, crispy sage, toasted pecans, and Parmesan.

Starting with refrigerated pumpkin ravioli means this cozy dinner can be on the table in about 20 minutes. Pair it with roasted vegetables or a simple green salad for an easy fall meal that feels extra special.

Get the Pumpkin Ravioli with Brown Butter Sauce recipe

10. Baked Pumpkin Macaroni and Cheese

Here’s an easy way to introduce pumpkin to kids who might not be ready for pumpkin pie or pumpkin muffins.

This Baked Pumpkin Macaroni and Cheese combines pumpkin puree with cheddar, Parmesan, Greek yogurt, and pasta for a creamy, comforting family dinner. The pumpkin blends right into the cheesy sauce while adding extra creaminess.

Get the Baked Pumpkin Macaroni and Cheese recipe

11. Pumpkin Chili

Pumpkin might be a surprising chili ingredient, but it works beautifully in this hearty vegetarian dinner.

Our Pumpkin Chili combines pumpkin puree with quinoa, butternut squash, tomatoes, and three kinds of beans. The pumpkin adds richness and a subtle sweetness without giving the chili an overpowering pumpkin flavor.

Pile on your favorite chili toppings and serve it with cornbread or tortilla chips for the ultimate chilly-night dinner.

Get the Pumpkin Chili recipe

12. Creamy Pumpkin Soup

There are few things cozier than a warm bowl of soup on a crisp fall evening.

This Pumpkin Soup is creamy, mild, and comforting, making it a great family-friendly way to serve pumpkin in a savory dish. And because it uses convenient canned pumpkin puree, you can make it long after pumpkin-patch season is over.

Serve it with crusty bread, grilled cheese, or a simple sandwich for dipping.

Get the Pumpkin Soup recipe

13. Toasted Coconut Pumpkin Bread

Pumpkin bread gets a tropical twist in this Toasted Coconut Pumpkin Bread. Pumpkin puree and warm spices give it classic fall flavor while coconut oil and toasted coconut add something a little unexpected.

Made with a combination of whole wheat and all-purpose flour and sweetened with honey, this cozy quick bread makes a delicious breakfast, snack, or addition to a fall brunch.

Get the Toasted Coconut Pumpkin Bread recipe

14. Soft Pumpkin Cookies with Maple Frosting

These Soft Pumpkin Cookies with Maple Frosting are thick, cakey, warmly spiced, and incredibly easy to make. There’s no rolling, chilling, or cutting required—just scoop and bake.

The maple frosting makes them an especially fun fall treat, but you can leave the frosting off for a simpler snack.

They also freeze well, so consider making a double batch and saving some for later.

Get the Soft Pumpkin Cookies with Maple Frosting recipe

15. Pumpkin Mousse

Light, fluffy, and full of cozy fall flavor, this Pumpkin Mousse is a simple dessert that feels special enough for Thanksgiving but easy enough to make whenever a pumpkin craving hits.

Pumpkin puree is flavored with pumpkin pie spice, vanilla, and pure maple syrup, then folded with whipped cream for an airy texture. Serve it as-is or top it with whipped cream, chopped pecans, or crumbled graham crackers or gingersnaps.

Get the Pumpkin Mousse recipe

Why We Love Cooking with Pumpkin

Pumpkin is incredibly versatile. Its mild flavor works in both sweet and savory recipes, and canned pumpkin puree makes it one of the easiest vegetables to keep on hand.

You can stir it into pancake batter, oatmeal, muffins, soups, chili, pasta sauces, smoothies, dips, and baked goods. It’s also an easy way to add color, moisture, and creamy texture to family-friendly recipes.

Better yet, an open can of pumpkin doesn’t have to mean making pumpkin pie. A spoonful can go into oatmeal or smoothies, while larger amounts can become muffins, soup, chili, bread, or an easy pumpkin dip.

Pumpkin Puree vs. Pumpkin Pie Filling

When making most of these recipes, look for 100% pure pumpkin puree, not pumpkin pie filling.

Pumpkin puree is simply cooked and pureed pumpkin, so you control the sweetness and spices yourself. Pumpkin pie filling is already sweetened and seasoned, which can change the taste and texture of a recipe.

What Can I Do With Leftover Pumpkin Puree?

If your recipe doesn’t use the entire can, don’t throw the rest away.

Add leftover pumpkin to oatmeal, pancakes, waffles, muffins, smoothies, yogurt, dips, soups, or pasta sauce. Even a small amount can add extra moisture and subtle pumpkin flavor.

For easy portioning, spoon leftover puree into an ice cube tray and freeze it. Once frozen, transfer the pumpkin cubes to a freezer-safe container so you can grab a small amount whenever you need it.

Frequently Asked Questions About Pumpkin Recipes

What can I make with a can of pumpkin?

Pumpkin puree can be used for much more than pie. Try it in muffins, pancakes, waffles, oatmeal, smoothies, bread, cookies, dips, mousse, hummus, soup, chili, macaroni and cheese, or pasta dishes.

Are canned pumpkin and pumpkin puree the same thing?

Usually, yes. A can labeled 100% pure pumpkin contains pumpkin puree and can be used in recipes that call for canned pumpkin. Just make sure you aren’t buying pumpkin pie filling, which contains added sweeteners and spices.

Can you use pumpkin in savory recipes?

Absolutely! Pumpkin’s mild sweetness pairs especially well with sage, cheese, beans, quinoa, warm spices, and pasta. Pumpkin ravioli, pumpkin chili, pumpkin soup, hummus, and pumpkin macaroni and cheese are all great ways to move beyond sweet pumpkin recipes.

What spices go well with pumpkin?

For sweet recipes, pumpkin pairs beautifully with cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves, and allspice. For savory dishes, try sage, garlic, cumin, paprika, chili powder, black pepper, or Parmesan.

What are good pumpkin recipes for kids?

Start with familiar foods your kids already enjoy. Pumpkin pancakes, waffles, muffins, oatmeal, mac and cheese, dips, and soft pumpkin cookies can all be approachable ways to introduce pumpkin.

If your kids aren’t sure about pumpkin yet, remember that repeated exposure counts. They don’t have to love every pumpkin recipe the first time they try it.

More Pumpkin, Please!

Whether you’re looking for a cozy breakfast, an easy weeknight dinner, a lunchbox snack, or something sweet to celebrate fall, these healthy pumpkin recipes make it easy to put that can of pumpkin to good use.

Start the morning with pumpkin pancakes or scones, warm up with pumpkin chili or soup for dinner, and finish the day with pumpkin mousse or a soft pumpkin cookie. Pumpkin season never lasts quite long enough—so we might as well make the most of it!
